part.formularios.title: Accessible Forms
part.formularios.summary: Forms are one of the areas with the most accessibility problems. The basic principles are:
sec.formularios.label.title: Label
sec.formularios.label.summary: Every field needs a label associated with it. Without one, the screen reader announces only "edit field" and the person has no idea what to type.
The placeholder disappears as soon as typing starts, and screen reader support for it is inconsistent. It is a hint, never the label.
The placeholder disappears while the field is being filled in.
Screen readers may also behave inconsistently when it is the only source of the name.
sec.formularios.campos-obrigatorios.summ: The required condition has to be announced, not just shown with an asterisk. Native required already does it; aria-required reinforces it.
sec.formularios.mensagens-de-ajuda.title: Help Messages
sec.formularios.mensagens-de-ajuda.summa: aria-describedby ties a hint to the field, so the screen reader reads the name and then the description.
sec.formularios.validacao-de-erro.title: Error Validation
sec.formularios.validacao-de-erro.summar: aria-invalid marks the field as failing validation, so the state is announced along with the name.
The error message must be connected to the field it belongs to. Loose text on screen is invisible to whoever is on the field.

Tax ID
Invalid field
Invalid tax ID
sec.formularios.erro-dinamico-com-aria-l: An error that appears after submission needs a live region, otherwise nobody using a screen reader learns that it exists.
part.fundamentos.title: Angular Accessibility Fundamentals
part.fundamentos.summary: First part of the accessibility documentation for Angular applications, VoiceOver and TalkBack.
sec.fundamentos.o-que-e-acessibilidade.s: Accessibility is a digital product being usable by everyone, regardless of visual, hearing, motor, cognitive or temporary limitations.
sec.fundamentos.o-que-e-acessibilidade.0: Accessibility is the capacity of a digital product to be used by every person, regardless of visual, hearing, motor, cognitive or temporary limitations.
sec.fundamentos.o-que-e-acessibilidade.1: A person with low vision using zoom.
A person with reduced mobility using the keyboard.
A person with a cognitive disability.
A person with an injured arm using only one hand.
sec.fundamentos.wcag-2-2.title: WCAG 2.2
sec.fundamentos.wcag-2-2.summary: WCAG is the most widely used standard in the world for evaluating digital accessibility. AA is the level most companies target.
sec.fundamentos.wcag-2-2.0.text: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is the most widely used set of guidelines in the world for evaluating digital accessibility.
sec.fundamentos.pour.title: POUR
sec.fundamentos.pour.summary: Every WCAG criterion comes from four pillars: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable and Robust.
sec.fundamentos.pour.0.text: Every WCAG criterion derives from four pillars:
sec.fundamentos.pour.2.item.0: The user has to be able to perceive the content.
sec.fundamentos.pour.2.item.2: Information cannot depend on colour alone.
sec.fundamentos.pour.4.item.0: The interface has to be usable.
sec.fundamentos.leitores-de-tela-2.title: Screen readers
sec.fundamentos.leitores-de-tela-2.summa: TalkBack on Android, VoiceOver on iOS. Both need three things to work: an accessible name, the right role, and the right state.
sec.fundamentos.leitores-de-tela-2.1.tex: The native screen reader on Android.
sec.fundamentos.leitores-de-tela-2.3.tex: The native screen reader on iOS.
sec.fundamentos.leitores-de-tela-2.4.tex: What do they need in order to work correctly?
sec.fundamentos.como-um-leitor-de-tela-e: How does a screen reader see a page?
Not the way sighted users do. They move through headings, buttons, links, fields and landmarks — a visually perfect screen can be unusable.
These users do not see the interface the way sighted users do.
A visually perfect screen can be completely unusable with a screen reader.
sec.fundamentos.regra-de-ouro-da-acessib: Semantic HTML first, ARIA second. If a native tag solves the problem, use it — you get role, keyboard and state for free.
Always prefer semantic HTML before reaching for ARIA.
If a native HTML tag can solve the problem, use it.
sec.fundamentos.estrutura-semantica-basi: header, nav, main and footer give a screen reader the map of the page before a single line is read.
sec.fundamentos.landmarks.title: Landmarks
sec.fundamentos.landmarks.summary: Landmarks let screen readers jump straight to the important regions of the page instead of reading through everything.
sec.fundamentos.landmarks.0.text: Landmarks let screen readers navigate quickly through the important regions of the page.
sec.fundamentos.headings.title: Headings
sec.fundamentos.headings.summary: Headings form a navigation tree. Skipping a level suggests a structure that does not exist and disorients the reader.
sec.fundamentos.accessible-name.title: Accessible Name
sec.fundamentos.accessible-name.summary: Every interactive element needs a name. It comes from visible text, or from aria-label when there is no text to use.
sec.fundamentos.accessible-name.0.text: Every interactive element must have an accessible name.
sec.fundamentos.accessible-description.s: aria-describedby adds a hint alongside the name. The screen reader reads the field name and then the description.
sec.fundamentos.accessible-description.1: The screen reader will combine the field name with its description.
sec.fundamentos.nome-role-estado.title: Name + Role + State
sec.fundamentos.nome-role-estado.summary: Almost every screen reader problem comes down to three questions: what is the name, what is the role, what is the state.
sec.fundamentos.nome-role-estado.0.text: Almost any screen reader analysis can be reduced to three questions:
sec.fundamentos.erros-mais-comuns-encont: The most common mistakes in Angular
Clickable divs, unlabelled icon buttons, placeholder-only inputs, missing headings, modals without focus management, and positive tabindex.
A clickable div pretending to be a button.
A clickable icon with no aria-label.
An input with only a placeholder.
A modal with no focus management.
Form errors that are never announced.
sec.fundamentos.mentalidade-para-o-time-: A mindset for the Angular team
Five questions to ask before building any component — they catch most accessibility problems before a single line is written.
Is there a native HTML tag for this?
Does the element have an accessible name?
Does it work with the keyboard?
part.aria.title: Complete ARIA for Angular
part.aria.summary: Everything an Angular developer normally reaches for day to day, for TalkBack, VoiceOver and WCAG.
sec.aria.o-que-e-aria.title: What is ARIA?
sec.aria.o-que-e-aria.summary: ARIA exists to complement HTML semantics, never to replace them. If a native tag solves it, use the native tag.
sec.aria.o-que-e-aria.2.text: ARIA exists to complement HTML semantics.
sec.aria.o-que-e-aria.3.cb.0.text: ARIA does NOT replace semantic HTML.
sec.aria.regra-de-ouro.title: The Golden Rule
sec.aria.regra-de-ouro.summary: No ARIA is better than bad ARIA. If native HTML already solves the problem, adding ARIA only creates room for it to go stale.
sec.aria.regra-de-ouro.1.text: If native HTML solves it, do not add ARIA for no reason.
sec.aria.accessible-name-2.title: Accessible Name
sec.aria.accessible-name-2.summary: Every interactive element needs a name. Inner text is the simplest source, and the one least likely to go out of date.
sec.aria.accessible-name-2.0.text: Every interactive element must have an accessible name.
sec.aria.aria-label.title: aria-label
sec.aria.aria-label.summary: Sets the accessible name when there is no visible text — icon-only buttons, actions without a label, custom elements.
sec.aria.aria-labelledby.title: aria-labelledby
sec.aria.aria-labelledby.summary: Uses another element on the page as the accessible name, by referencing its id. Useful when the label already exists as visible text.
sec.aria.aria-labelledby.0.r.0.1: Uses another element as the name.
sec.aria.aria-describedby.title: aria-describedby
sec.aria.aria-describedby.summary: Adds a description alongside the name. The screen reader reads the name first, then the description.
sec.aria.aria-hidden.title: aria-hidden
sec.aria.aria-hidden.summary: Hides an element from the accessibility tree. Never put it on something focusable — the Tab key still reaches it, but nothing is announced.
sec.aria.aria-hidden.0.r.0.1: Hides it from the screen reader.
sec.aria.aria-hidden.0.r.1.1: Exposes it to the screen reader.
sec.aria.aria-expanded.title: aria-expanded
sec.aria.aria-expanded.summary: Announces whether a control is expanded or collapsed. It has to track the real state — a stale value is worse than none.
sec.aria.aria-controls.title: aria-controls
sec.aria.aria-controls.summary: Connects a control to the content it operates, so the screen reader can offer a way to jump straight to it.
sec.aria.aria-controls.0.text: Connects a control to a piece of content.
sec.aria.aria-current.title: aria-current
sec.aria.aria-current.summary: Marks the current item within a set: the current page in a nav, the current step in a stepper, the current location in a breadcrumb.
sec.aria.aria-selected.title: aria-selected
sec.aria.aria-selected.summary: Announces which item is selected in a tab list, listbox or grid. Without it the screen reader says "tab" but never which one is active.
sec.aria.aria-checked.title: aria-checked
sec.aria.aria-checked.summary: Carries the checked state of a custom checkbox, radio or switch. A native input already does this on its own.
sec.aria.aria-pressed.title: aria-pressed
sec.aria.aria-pressed.summary: For toggle buttons — favourite, mute, bookmark. It tells the screen reader the button holds a state, not just an action.
sec.aria.aria-disabled.title: aria-disabled
sec.aria.aria-disabled.summary: Announces the control as unavailable while keeping it reachable by keyboard — unlike the native disabled attribute, which removes it from the tab order.
sec.aria.aria-required.title: aria-required
sec.aria.aria-required.summary: Announces that the field must be filled in. Native required already does it; use this when the control is not a native input.
sec.aria.aria-invalid.title: aria-invalid
sec.aria.aria-invalid.summary: Marks a field as failing validation, so the state is announced together with the name when the person reaches it.
sec.aria.aria-live.title: aria-live
sec.aria.aria-live.summary: Announces content that changes without a page load — toasts, results, status. Use polite; assertive interrupts whatever is being read.
sec.aria.aria-live.0.r.1.1: Announces when there is a pause.
sec.aria.aria-atomic.title: aria-atomic
sec.aria.aria-atomic.summary: Controls how much of a live region is re-read when part of it changes — the whole thing, or only what changed.
sec.aria.aria-busy.title: aria-busy
sec.aria.aria-busy.summary: Tells assistive technology that a region is still loading, so it holds off announcing a half-updated state.
sec.aria.aria-modal.title: aria-modal
sec.aria.aria-modal.summary: Tells the screen reader that everything behind the dialog is unavailable. Without it, the content underneath keeps being read.
sec.aria.aria-haspopup.title: aria-haspopup
sec.aria.aria-haspopup.summary: Announces that a control opens a menu, a dialog or a list — so the person knows what to expect before activating it.
sec.aria.aria-para-progress-bar.title: ARIA for a Progress Bar
sec.aria.aria-para-progress-bar.summary: role=progressbar needs valuemin, valuemax and valuenow together — otherwise the screen reader announces a bar with no number.
sec.aria.principais-roles.title: The roles you will actually use
sec.aria.principais-roles.summary: The handful of ARIA roles that cover almost every real case: button, link, dialog, alert, status, tabs, checkbox, switch, menu and listbox.
sec.aria.roles-que-voce-quase-nunca-prec: Roles you will almost never need
tree, treegrid, feed, math, meter, log and marquee. Reaching for these without a real need usually makes things worse.
Do not use them without a real need.
sec.aria.angular-attribute-binding.title: Angular Attribute Binding
sec.aria.angular-attribute-binding.summa: How to bind ARIA to a dynamic value in Angular, so the attribute tracks the real state instead of freezing at its initial value.
sec.aria.erros-mais-comuns-com-aria.summ: Redundant roles, unnecessary labels, aria-hidden on real content, live region overuse, and states that stop tracking the DOM.
sec.aria.erros-mais-comuns-com-aria.0.it: Adding an aria-label that is not needed.
An aria-expanded state that stops tracking reality.
aria-describedby pointing at an id that does not exist.
Building a custom component with no keyboard support.
sec.aria.checklist-aria.title: ARIA Checklist
sec.aria.checklist-aria.summary: Six questions to run over any element carrying ARIA, before calling it done.
sec.aria.checklist-aria.0.item.0: Does it have an accessible name?
sec.aria.checklist-aria.0.item.1: Does it have the correct role?
sec.aria.checklist-aria.0.item.2: Does it have the correct state?
sec.aria.checklist-aria.0.item.3: Is it in sync with the DOM?
part.componentes.title: Interactive Components and Complex Structures
part.componentes.summary: This part covers the components that produce the most accessibility bugs in Angular applications.
sec.componentes.botoes.title: Buttons
sec.componentes.botoes.summary: Use a real button. A clickable div loses the role, the keyboard, the state and the semantics all at once.
sec.componentes.botao-apenas-com-icone.s: Without a label, the screen reader announces just "button". The person knows a control exists but not what it does.
sec.componentes.links.title: Links
sec.componentes.links.summary: Links navigate, buttons perform actions. Swapping them confuses anyone who relies on the announced role to know what will happen.
sec.componentes.cards-clicaveis.title: Clickable Cards
sec.componentes.cards-clicaveis.summary: Wrap the card in a real button or anchor. A div with a click handler is invisible to the keyboard.
sec.componentes.accordion.title: Accordion
sec.componentes.accordion.summary: The trigger needs aria-expanded and aria-controls, so the state is announced along with the name.
sec.componentes.accordion.1.text:
How does it work?
Button
Collapsed
sec.componentes.accordion-com-angular.su: Bind aria-expanded to the real state. A hard-coded value announces "collapsed" forever, even with the panel open.
aria-expanded has to reflect the real state.
sec.componentes.tabs.title: Tabs
sec.componentes.tabs.summary: role=tablist with aria-selected on each tab. Without it the screen reader says "tab" but never which one is active.
sec.componentes.tab-panel.title: Tab Panel
sec.componentes.tab-panel.summary: The panel that holds the content of the selected tab, tied to it so the reader can move between the two.
sec.componentes.modal.title: Modal
sec.componentes.modal.summary: role=dialog, aria-modal and a label. Without aria-modal the screen reader keeps reading the content behind it.
sec.componentes.checklist-modal.title: Modal Checklist
sec.componentes.checklist-modal.summary: Six things every modal has to do: role, aria-modal, take focus, trap focus, close on ESC, and give focus back.
sec.componentes.checklist-modal.0.item.2: Does it receive focus when it opens?
sec.componentes.checklist-modal.0.item.5: Does it return focus when it closes?
sec.componentes.bottom-sheet.title: Bottom Sheet
sec.componentes.bottom-sheet.summary: It is a modal that happens to slide up from the bottom. Same rules apply, without exception.
sec.componentes.menu.title: Menu
sec.componentes.menu.summary: The trigger announces that it opens a menu, through aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.
sec.componentes.itens-de-menu.title: Menu Items
sec.componentes.itens-de-menu.summary: Each item carries role=menuitem, and the whole set has to be reachable with the arrow keys.
sec.componentes.dropdown.title: Dropdown
sec.componentes.dropdown.summary: Prefer the native select whenever possible. It comes with keyboard, state and mobile behaviour already correct.
sec.componentes.dropdown.0.text: Whenever possible, prefer the native select.
sec.componentes.combobox.title: Combobox
sec.componentes.combobox.summary: One of the hardest patterns to build correctly. Since Angular v22 there is an official answer: ngCombobox from @angular/aria.
sec.componentes.combobox.1.text: Complex to implement. Avoid building it by hand — see Angular Aria.
sec.componentes.lista.title: List
sec.componentes.lista.summary: A real ul or ol makes the screen reader announce "list with N items", which tells the person how much is ahead.
sec.componentes.breadcrumb.title: Breadcrumb
sec.componentes.breadcrumb.summary: A labelled nav, with aria-current="page" on the current item so it is announced as where you are.
sec.componentes.stepper.title: Stepper
sec.componentes.stepper.summary: aria-current="step" marks the current step, so the person knows where they are in the flow without seeing the highlight.
sec.componentes.tabela-simples.title: Simple Table
sec.componentes.tabela-simples.summary: caption, th and scope are what let the screen reader tie each cell to its header instead of reading loose numbers.
sec.componentes.tabela-boas-praticas.sum: Use caption, th and scope, and never build a table out of divs — it destroys the relationship between cell and header.
sec.componentes.tabela-boas-praticas.0.i: Avoid tables built out of divs.
sec.componentes.tooltip.title: Tooltip
sec.componentes.tooltip.summary: Tie it with aria-describedby, and make it open on focus too — a tooltip that only responds to hover does not exist for the keyboard.
sec.componentes.toast.title: Toast
sec.componentes.toast.summary: role=status announces the message without stealing focus, which is what you want for a confirmation.
sec.componentes.snackbar.title: Snackbar
sec.componentes.snackbar.summary: A polite live region: it announces when there is a pause, instead of cutting off whatever is being read.
sec.componentes.alertas-criticos.title: Critical Alerts
sec.componentes.alertas-criticos.summary: role=alert interrupts immediately. Reserve it for what genuinely cannot wait — everything else is noise.
sec.componentes.loading.title: Loading
sec.componentes.loading.summary: aria-busy tells assistive technology the region is still updating, so it does not announce a half-finished state.
sec.componentes.progress-bar.title: Progress Bar
sec.componentes.progress-bar.summary: role=progressbar needs valuemin, valuemax and valuenow, otherwise the bar is announced with no number attached.
sec.componentes.skeleton-loading.title: Skeleton Loading
sec.componentes.skeleton-loading.summary: The placeholder shapes carry no information. Hide them with aria-hidden so the screen reader is not read a wall of nothing.
sec.componentes.skeleton-loading.0.text: The visual placeholder should be ignored by the screen reader.
sec.componentes.carrossel.title: Carousel
sec.componentes.carrossel.summary: Needs previous, next and pause controls, and slides that can be identified. Auto-rotation without a pause is a WCAG failure.
sec.componentes.infinite-scroll.title: Infinite Scroll
sec.componentes.infinite-scroll.summary: Announce the newly loaded items, keep focus where it was, and avoid the page jumping under the person.
sec.componentes.drag-and-drop.title: Drag and Drop
sec.componentes.drag-and-drop.summary: Never rely on the gesture alone. There has to be a click or keyboard path to the same result.
sec.componentes.drag-and-drop.0.text: Never rely on the gesture alone.
sec.componentes.drag-and-drop.1.text: Always offer a click or keyboard alternative.
sec.componentes.upload-de-arquivo.title: File Upload
sec.componentes.upload-de-arquivo.summar: A native file input with a real label. Custom upload widgets are a common place to lose the keyboard entirely.
sec.componentes.mensagens-dinamicas.summ: Anything that changes without a page load needs a live region: toasts, applied filters, finished searches, approved payments.
sec.componentes.checklist-de-componentes: Nine questions to run over any component before calling it done — name, role, state, keyboard, focus and announcements.
Does it have an accessible name?
Does it have the correct role?
Does it have the correct state?
Does it work with the keyboard?
Does it keep a sensible focus order?
part.angular.title: Angular, Angular Material and Angular CDK A11y
part.angular.summary: This part covers the practices specific to Angular, Angular Material and the Angular CDK.
sec.angular.angular-e-acessivel-por-padr: No. Angular renders the HTML you write. Good HTML tends to produce an accessible app; bad HTML is not fixed by the framework.
Angular renders the HTML you write. If the HTML is accessible, the application tends to be accessible. If the HTML is bad, Angular does not fix it.
sec.angular.regra-principal-para-angular: Semantic HTML first, ARIA second. A button with a click handler beats a div with a click handler, every time.
sec.angular.binding-de-aria.title: Binding ARIA
sec.angular.binding-de-aria.summary: Use attribute binding when the ARIA value is dynamic, so it tracks the real state instead of freezing at its initial value.
sec.angular.ngif-e-foco.title: NgIf and Focus
sec.angular.ngif-e-foco.summary: One of the most common bugs: when an element leaves the DOM, the focus that was on it disappears with no replacement.
sec.angular.ngif-e-foco.0.text: One of the most common problems.
sec.angular.ngif-e-foco.2.text: When the element leaves the DOM, focus can be lost.
sec.angular.ngfor-e-acessibilidade.title: NgFor and Accessibility
sec.angular.ngfor-e-acessibilidade.summa: Repeat inside a real list. A loop of divs loses the "list with N items" announcement that orients the reader.
sec.angular.router-angular.title: The Angular Router
sec.angular.router-angular.summary: SPAs do not reload the page, so the screen reader has no idea the screen changed. This is the single biggest accessibility gap in Angular apps.
sec.angular.router-angular.0.text: SPA applications do not reload the page.
sec.angular.router-angular.1.text: The screen reader does not automatically notice that the screen changed.
sec.angular.foco-apos-navegacao.title: Focus after navigation
sec.angular.foco-apos-navegacao.summary: After each route change, move focus to the h1 or to the main content. Otherwise focus stays where the old page was.
sec.angular.exemplo-de-destino-de-foco.s: Give the heading tabindex="-1" so it can receive focus programmatically without entering the tab order.
sec.angular.anunciar-mudancas-de-tela.su: Announce the name of the new screen after navigating. Announce after moving focus — the reverse order cuts the announcement short.
In Angular applications it is common to announce the name of the screen.
sec.angular.angular-cdk-accessibility.su: The most important accessibility package in the Angular stack: LiveAnnouncer, FocusMonitor, FocusTrap, FocusKeyManager and InteractivityChecker.
The most important package for accessibility in the Angular stack.
sec.angular.liveannouncer.title: LiveAnnouncer
sec.angular.liveannouncer.summary: Announces a message to screen readers programmatically, through a managed live region — no markup of your own required.
sec.angular.liveannouncer.0.text: Lets you create announcements for screen readers.
sec.angular.quando-usar-liveannouncer.su: For outcomes that happen without a page change: payment completed, filter applied, search finished, upload done, an error that matters.
sec.angular.cdktrapfocus.title: cdkTrapFocus
sec.angular.cdktrapfocus.summary: Keeps Tab inside a region. Essential for modals, bottom sheets and dialogs, where focus escaping to the page behind breaks everything.
sec.angular.exemplo-cdktrapfocus.title: cdkTrapFocus example
sec.angular.exemplo-cdktrapfocus.summary: One directive on the container is enough to keep Tab cycling inside it.
sec.angular.focusmonitor.title: FocusMonitor
sec.angular.focusmonitor.summary: Tells you how focus arrived — mouse, keyboard, touch or programmatically. Useful for showing the focus ring only when it helps.
sec.angular.focusmonitor.0.text: Identifies how focus reached the element.
sec.angular.focuskeymanager.title: FocusKeyManager
sec.angular.focuskeymanager.summary: Handles arrow key navigation inside a set of items — tabs, menus, listboxes and comboboxes.
sec.angular.angular-material.title: Angular Material
sec.angular.angular-material.summary: Material implements much of the accessibility for you — which does not mean the result is accessible without testing it.
sec.angular.angular-material.0.text: Material already implements a good part of the accessibility.
sec.angular.angular-material.1.text: It still has to be tested.
sec.angular.matdialog.title: MatDialog
sec.angular.matdialog.summary: Brings the dialog role, focus management, ESC and a backdrop already implemented.
sec.angular.checklist-matdialog.title: MatDialog Checklist
sec.angular.checklist-matdialog.summary: Four things to confirm even with MatDialog: a title, focus in, focus back, and a close button.
sec.angular.checklist-matdialog.0.item.3: Does it have a close button?
sec.angular.mattabs.title: MatTabs
sec.angular.mattabs.summary: Implements the tab structure. Still confirm the arrow keys work and that both screen readers announce the selected tab.
sec.angular.matmenu.title: MatMenu
sec.angular.matmenu.summary: Prefer MatMenu over a hand-rolled menu. Keyboard navigation in menus is easy to get subtly wrong.
sec.angular.matmenu.0.text: Prefer building menus with MatMenu rather than a homemade implementation.
sec.angular.matselect.title: MatSelect
sec.angular.matselect.summary: The component most prone to accessibility bugs. Always test opening, closing, option announcement and selected state.
sec.angular.matselect.0.text: The component most prone to accessibility bugs.
sec.angular.matexpansionpanel.title: MatExpansionPanel
sec.angular.matexpansionpanel.summary: The Material accordion. Check aria-expanded, where focus goes, and whether the state change is announced.
sec.angular.mattable.title: MatTable
sec.angular.mattable.summary: Do not assume a Material table is automatically accessible. Check the caption, the headers, sorting and focus.
sec.angular.mattable.0.text: Do not assume every Material table is automatically accessible.
sec.angular.overlay-components.title: Overlay Components
sec.angular.overlay-components.summary: Anything that opens over the screen deserves extra attention: modal, popover, tooltip, select, menu and datepicker.
sec.angular.overlay-components.0.text: Every component that opens over the screen deserves extra attention.
sec.angular.datepicker.title: Datepicker
sec.angular.datepicker.summary: Check keyboard navigation and how the day, month and year are announced. Date pickers fail quietly for keyboard users.
sec.angular.loading-angular.title: Loading in Angular
sec.angular.loading-angular.summary: State changes have to be announced. A spinner that only spins tells nothing to anyone using a screen reader.
sec.angular.loading-angular.0.text: State changes have to be announced.
sec.angular.lazy-loading.title: Lazy Loading
sec.angular.lazy-loading.summary: When content appears after an async load, decide deliberately where focus goes and what gets announced.
sec.angular.lazy-loading.0.text: When content appears after an asynchronous load, focus and announcement both have to be considered.
sec.angular.signals-e-acessibilidade.sum: Signals update the UI automatically, but screen readers are not notified automatically. Use aria-live or LiveAnnouncer.
sec.angular.signals-e-acessibilidade.1.t: But screen readers are not notified automatically.
sec.angular.standalone-components.title: Standalone Components
sec.angular.standalone-components.summar: No accessibility differences of their own. The same rules apply exactly as before.
sec.angular.pipes.title: Pipes
sec.angular.pipes.summary: Formatting can hurt how something is read aloud. Check how currency, dates and numbers are actually announced.
sec.angular.pipes.0.text: Be careful with formatting that harms how the value is read.
sec.angular.pipes.3.text: Check how the screen reader announces it.
sec.angular.custom-components.title: Custom Components

sec.angular.angular-aria.title: Angular Aria
sec.angular.angular-aria.summary: The official @angular/aria package, shipped with Angular v22: headless directives implementing the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.
sec.angular.angular-aria.0.text: In November 2025, with Angular v22, the Angular team released the official Angular Aria package.
sec.angular.angular-aria.2.text: These are headless directives implementing the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns. They handle keyboard navigation, ARIA attributes, focus management and screen reader support. You provide the HTML and the styling.
sec.angular.angular-aria.3.cb.0.text: This is the most significant accessibility release in Angular's history. Combobox, listbox, menu and tree are the components that produce the most accessibility bugs when hand-rolled — and now there is an official implementation, maintained by the framework team, following the specification.
sec.angular.angular-aria.4.text: Before it, the answer to "I need an accessible combobox" was "the implementation is complex, avoid building it by hand" — with nothing offered in its place. Now there is an answer.
sec.angular.padroes-do-angular-aria.summ: Thirteen patterns, from combobox to grid. Compare the list with the components that produce the most accessibility bugs — it is nearly the same list.
A text input coordinated with a popup.
A list of options, single or multiple selection.
A hierarchical list with expand and collapse.
sec.angular.padroes-do-angular-aria.2.te: Compare this with the list of components that produce the most accessibility bugs in Angular. It is almost the same list.
sec.angular.angular-aria-material-ou-cdk: The three coexist and solve different problems: styled components, unstyled behaviour, and low-level utilities.
The three coexist and solve different problems.
The Material look works for the product.
Your own design system, without reimplementing keyboard and ARIA.
LiveAnnouncer, FocusTrap and FocusMonitor in any scenario.
The CDK A11y package is still needed even when using Angular Aria. Announcing "payment completed" with LiveAnnouncer is not a widget pattern.
sec.angular.o-que-o-angular-aria-nao-res: What Angular Aria does not solve
It covers widget patterns. Most production accessibility bugs are clickable divs, unlabelled icons and lost focus — none of which it touches.
The library solves widget patterns. Most accessibility bugs in production are not complex widgets.
A clickable div instead of a button.
A clickable icon with no accessible name.
An input with only a placeholder.
A form error that is never announced.
Focus lost after a route change.
An image with no alternative text.
A table with no associated headers.

Headless directive means you provide the HTML and the CSS. You can use Angular Aria and still ship an inaccessible screen: invisible focus, poor contrast, DOM order that does not match the visual order.
The library removes one class of error. It does not replace knowing the subject, nor testing with TalkBack and VoiceOver.

part.leitores-de-tela.title: TalkBack, VoiceOver and Real Testing
part.leitores-de-tela.summary: This part focuses on how screen readers actually behave. Plenty of components are technically correct in the HTML and still deliver a poor experience.
sec.leitores-de-tela.principio-fundament: Screen readers rely on name, role and state. Almost every bug can be diagnosed through those three questions.
Almost every bug can be analysed through those three points.
A plain button announces its name and its role. Both TalkBack and VoiceOver say the same thing here.
sec.leitores-de-tela.botao-com-icone.sum: Without a label the announcement is just "button". With aria-label it becomes the action the person is about to take.
sec.leitores-de-tela.campos-obrigatorios: The required condition is announced along with the field, so the person knows before typing rather than after submitting.
sec.leitores-de-tela.campo-invalido.summ: aria-invalid makes the failure part of what the screen reader says when focus lands on the field.
sec.leitores-de-tela.checkbox.title: Checkbox
sec.leitores-de-tela.checkbox.summary: A native checkbox announces the label, the role and the state — and updates the state on its own when toggled.

sec.leitores-de-tela.switch.title: Switch
sec.leitores-de-tela.switch.summary: role=switch with aria-checked announces on and off, which reads more naturally than checked and unchecked for a toggle.
sec.leitores-de-tela.accordion-2.title: Accordion
sec.leitores-de-tela.accordion-2.summary: The announcement has to change when the panel opens. If it always says "collapsed", aria-expanded is not bound to the real state.
sec.leitores-de-tela.tabs-2.title: Tabs
sec.leitores-de-tela.tabs-2.summary: The selected tab is announced as selected. Without aria-selected the person hears "tab" and cannot tell which one is active.
sec.leitores-de-tela.stepper-2.title: Stepper
sec.leitores-de-tela.stepper-2.summary: aria-current="step" turns a visual highlight into something the screen reader can convey.
sec.leitores-de-tela.mensagens-dinamicas: A live region announces on its own, without moving focus — which is exactly what you want for a confirmation.
Focus does not need to move.
The screen reader announces it automatically.
sec.leitores-de-tela.role-alert.title: role="alert"
sec.leitores-de-tela.role-alert.summary: Interrupts whatever is being read. Reserve it for what genuinely cannot wait — everything else becomes noise.
sec.leitores-de-tela.role-alert.2.text: Use it only for messages that matter.
sec.leitores-de-tela.foco-visivel.title: Visible Focus
sec.leitores-de-tela.foco-visivel.summar: Every focusable element has to show that it has focus. Removing the outline without a replacement is the equivalent of hiding the mouse cursor.
sec.leitores-de-tela.foco-visivel.0.text: Every focusable element must visually indicate that it received focus.
sec.leitores-de-tela.sequencia-de-foco.s: DOM order has to match visual order. Screen reader users move through the structure of the page, not through the layout.
sec.leitores-de-tela.sequencia-de-foco.0: The DOM order has to reflect the visual order.
sec.leitores-de-tela.sequencia-de-foco.1: Screen reader users navigate by following the structure of the page.
sec.leitores-de-tela.modais.title: Modals
sec.leitores-de-tela.modais.summary: On open: focus moves in, the content behind becomes unreachable, Tab stays inside. On close: focus returns to whatever opened it.
sec.leitores-de-tela.modais.3.item.0: Focus returns to the element that opened it.
sec.leitores-de-tela.problema-classico.s: The modal closes and focus vanishes to the top of the document. It has to go back to the button that opened it.
sec.leitores-de-tela.problema-classico.1: When the modal closes, focus often disappears.
sec.leitores-de-tela.problema-classico.2: It should return to the Edit button.
sec.leitores-de-tela.loading-2.title: Loading
sec.leitores-de-tela.loading-2.summary: Announce that something started and that it finished. Silence during a wait is indistinguishable from a broken page.
sec.leitores-de-tela.loading-2.0.text: Do not leave the user without feedback.
sec.leitores-de-tela.talkback-x-voiceove: The two differ in predictable places: forms, tabs, modals and selects. Testing on one does not cover the other.
Small differences in what gets announced.
The order of the announcement can vary.

sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.s: Enforceable across the EU since 28 June 2025. Accessibility stopped being an improvement and became a condition of entry.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.0: Since 28 June 2025 the European Accessibility Act has been enforceable in every country of the European Union.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.1: It is no longer only a concern for companies selling into Europe. Companies that serve European customers, or sit in the supply chain of a European company, fall within scope.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.4: Conformance is assessed against EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG. Version 4.1.1 is expected in 2026.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.5: In practice, meeting WCAG 2.2 level AA covers most of what the standard requires for web content. It is the same target this entire guide is aiming at.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.7: Accessibility stops being an improvement and becomes a condition of entry.

sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.sum: It affects more people than visual or motor impairment and gets a fraction of the attention. An interface that works for someone exhausted works better for everyone.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.0.t: Most accessibility effort goes to visual and motor impairment. Cognitive disability affects more people and receives less attention.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.1.t: This covers dyslexia, ADHD, autism, anxiety and age-related cognitive decline — and also temporary states: tiredness, being in a hurry, stress, using a phone in the middle of the street.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.2.c: An interface that works for someone exhausted works better for everyone. This is the clearest case that accessibility is not an edge case.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.4.i: Direct language, short sentences, no unnecessary jargon.
A visible step indicator in long flows.
Errors that say what to do, not just what is wrong.
Destructive actions with confirmation and undo.
No time limit, or the option to extend it.
Not depending on memory between steps.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.6.i: Automatic movement, a carousel that rotates on its own.
A long form with no sections and no partial saving.
A session that expires with no warning.

sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.title: The mindset that matters
sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.summary: The question is not whether the screen passed WCAG. It is whether a person using TalkBack or VoiceOver can finish the journey on their own.
sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.4.text: If the answer is yes, the implementation is usually on the right track.
